Article I. City Employee-Interests in Contract*
*Prior history: Prior code §§ 53.01.001-53.01.008.
2.16.010   Prohibition on city employee interest in city contract.
   A.   No city employee shall engage in any employment, activity, or
enterprise from which the employee receives compensation or in which the
employee has a financial interest and which is funded, all or in part, by the
city or any city department through or by a city contract unless the
employment, activity, or enterprise is required as a condition of the
employee's regular city employment. No city employee shall contract on his or
her own individual behalf as an independent contractor with the city or any
city department to provide services or goods.
   B.   This section shall not prohibit the city from entering into contracts
with an entity in which a city employee has a financial interest because of his
or her spouse's or dependent's employment with the entity, ownership or control
of the entity or other financial interest in the entity, provided that the
employee: (1) does not participate in the control or operation, or otherwise
participate or engage in the business or enterprise of, the entity; (2)
abstains from all participation in the making of the contract, pursuant to
Government_Code Section 1090 et seq.; and (3) if required by Section
2.16.030(G)(2) of this article, provides the notice required by that section.
(Ord. 2007-043 § 1)
2.16.020   Employees defined.
   For purposes of this article, a person shall be deemed to be an employee of
the city only if, during the previous twelve (12) month period, the employee
has worked one thousand forty (1,040) hours or more for the city. (Ord. 2007-
043 § 1)
2.16.030   Exception-Party to employment and other specified contracts.
   Section
2.16.010 shall not prohibit the following contracts:
   A.   A contract of employment in which the employee agrees to perform
services for the city as an employee of the city;
   B.   A contract in which the employee is a third-party beneficiary of an
agreement executed pursuant to the Meyers-Milias-Brown Act;
   C.   A contract in which the employee is to be reimbursed for actual and
necessary expenses incurred in the performance of an official duty as an
employee of the city;
   D.   A contract affecting retirement benefits paid or to be payable to an
employee as a present or future retired employee of the city;
   E.   A contract with the city for the off-duty employment of peace officers;
   F.   A contract with the city pursuant to which the employee pays for and
receives public services generally provided by the city to the public at large
if the terms and conditions of said contract are the same as if the employee
were not an employee of the city;
   G.   A contract in which the employee has only a remote financial interest.
      1.   Definition. For purposes of this provision, an employee has a remote
financial interest in a contract if the employee's interest is one of the
following:
         a.   That of a non-salaried officer of a nonprofit corporation or
association;
         b.   That of the owner of real property who enters into any agreement
with the city concerning that property pursuant to state or local land use
regulations;
         c.   That of the owner of real property whose interest is being
acquired by the city under the threat of or pursuant to the exercise of the
power of eminent domain.
      2.   The interest of an employee in any contract described in subsection
(G)(1) of this section shall be considered as being other than a remote
interest if the contract is one in which the employee has a supervisory
interest. An employee has a supervisory interest in a contract if the employee
is directly involved as an employee of the city in any of the following
activities in reference to said contract:
         a.   The preparation of contract plans or specifications;
         b.   The solicitation of bids for or the award of the contract;
         c.   The supervision or monitoring of performance under the contract.
      3.   Exception-Notice and Abstention. An employee of the city shall not
be considered as having a supervisory interest in a contract if, prior to
engaging in any of the activities described in subsection (G)(2) of this
section, the employee has notified his or her immediate city supervisor of the
interest in the contract and thereafter abstains from performance of these
duties in reference to the contract. (Ord. 2007-043 § 1)
2.16.040   Exception-Contract for public services.
   The provisions of this article shall not apply to any contract with the city
wherein any employee pays for and receives public services generally provided
by the city to the public at large if the terms and conditions of said contract
are the same as if the employee were not an employee of the city. (Ord. 2007-
043 § 1)
2.16.050   Violation-Penalty.
   Any employee who violates this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and
shall be subject to discipline by the city manager or other official in whom is
vested the disciplinary power. (Ord. 2007-043 § 1)
2.16.060   Contracts voidable.
   Any contract entered into in violation of this article shall be voidable at
the option of the city. (Ord. 2007-043 § 1)
Article II. Former Officers and Employees-Disqualification
2.16.090   Disqualification of former officers and employees in matters
connected with former official responsibilities.
   A.   No former officer or employee of the city shall, within one year after
his or her city employment has ceased, appear personally before the city
council or any department, board or commission or committee of the city as an
agent for anyone other than the city in connection with any proceeding,
application, request for ruling or other determination, contract, claim,
controversy or other matter which was under his or her official responsibility
as an officer or employee of the city at any time within one year prior to the
termination of such responsibility.
   B.   As used herein, the phrase "official responsibility" means the
authority, whether intermediate or final, whether exercisable alone or with
others and whether exercisable personally or through subordinates to approve,
disapprove or make recommendations for approval or disapproval to the city
council, any city board or commission, or any city department or division head
in connection with any proceeding, application, request for ruling or other
determination, contract, claim, controversy or other matter before the city.
   C.   As used herein, "officer" means any department head, assistant
department head and any division head or assistant division head.
   D.   As used herein, "employee" means any person whose position is included
in the classified service, and any employee whose position is by resolution
designated exempt from the classified service and which position is by
resolution also designated as "management." (Prior code § 53.02.010)
Article III. City Council and City Boards and Commissions
2.16.100   Applicability.
   Sections
2.16.110 through
2.16.150 apply to members of the city council, the following persons, and
members of the following boards, commissions, and bodies:
   Administration, Investment and Fiscal Management Board of the Sacramento
City Employees' Retirement System
   Civil Service Board
   Construction Code Advisory and Appeals Board
   Design director
   Housing Code Advisory and Appeals Board
   Planning and Design Commission
   Planning director
   Preservation Commission
   Preservation director
   Retirement Hearing Commission
   Sacramento City Public Facilities Financing Corporation
   Sacramento City Financing Authority
   Utilities Rate Advisory Commission
   Zoning administrator
(Ord. 2024-0040 § 1; Ord. 2012-048 § 1; Ord. 2012-004 § 5; Ord. 2008-001 § 2;
Ord. 2006-065 § 4; prior code § 53.03.020)
2.16.110   Disqualification.
   A.   Each city official shall disqualify him or herself from making or
participating in the making of any decision when he or she knows or in the
exercise of reasonable diligence should know that:
      1.   Another person, with whom the city official has an ownership
interest in real property or an investment in a business entity, is an
applicant or is principally involved in a matter before the board of which the
city official is a member; or
      2.   A family member is an applicant or is principally involved in a
matter before the board of which the city official is a member.
   No such city official shall be prevented from making or participating in the
making of any decision to the extent his or her participation is legally
required for the decision to be made.
   B.   No city official shall make or participate in making a decision on a
matter for which disqualification is required under subsection A of this
section. (Prior code § 53.03.021)
2.16.120   Manner of disqualification.
   A city official required to disqualify him or herself shall give notice of
disqualification at the meeting during which consideration of the decision
takes place. The notice of disqualification shall include the name of the
applicant or person principally involved in the matter before the board, and:
(1) whether the city official has an ownership interest in real property or an
investment in a business entity with such person, or (2) the name of the person
who is a family relative. Such notice shall be made part of the official record
of the board. The city official shall refrain from participation and shall not
attempt in any way to use his or her official position to influence any other
person with respect to the matter. (Prior code § 53.03.022)
2.16.130   Opinion of city attorney.
   Upon request, any city official who is unsure of any right or obligation
arising under this code may request a formal opinion or letter of advice from
the city attorney. If an opinion is rendered by the city attorney stating in
full the facts and the law upon which the opinion is based, compliance by the
city official may be evidence of good faith in any civil or criminal proceeding
brought pursuant to law. (Prior code § 53.03.023)
2.16.140   Definitions.
   For purposes of this article, the following terms shall have the meanings
specified:
   "Board" includes the city council and the boards and commissions listed in
Section
2.16.100 of this article.
   "Business entity" means any organization or enterprise operated for profit,
including, but not limited to, proprietorship, partnership, firm, business
trust, joint venture, syndicate, corporation, or association.
   "City official" and "city officials" includes the members of the city
council and members of the boards and commissions listed in Section
2.16.100 of this article.
   "Family relative" means and includes:
      1.   The spouse of a city official;
      2.   The parent or child or spouse of the parent or child of a city
official or of the spouse of a city official;
      3.   Any person or any spouse of any person related within the third
degree, inclusive of collateral consanguinity to any city official or the
spouse of any city official.
   Thus, the brother, sister, uncle, aunt, niece or nephew (and the spouse of
any of the foregoing) of a city official or of the spouse of a city official is
a family relative of the city official within the meaning of this code.
   Investment in business entity:
      1.   Includes any financial interest in or security issued by a business
entity, including, but not limited to, common stock, preferred stock, rights,
warrants, options, deed instruments and any partnership or other ownership
interest; and
      2.   Applies to any investment, regardless of where such business entity
is located or does business; and
      3.   Applies to a city official, if the official and the person who is an
applicant or is principally involved in the matter before such city official's
board each have a twenty-five thousand dollar ($25,000.00) or greater, or ten
(10) percent or greater, investment in such business entity.
   "Ownership interest in real property" means and includes any leasehold
beneficial or ownership interest or option to acquire such an interest in real
property regardless of where such property is located, if the city official and
the person who is an applicant or is principally involved in the matter before
such city official's board each have a twenty-five thousand dollar ($25,000.00)
or greater, or ten (10) percent or greater, interest in such property.
   "Principally involved" means and includes:
      1.   A person who has a twenty-five (25) percent or greater investment in
the business entity or a twenty-five (25) percent or greater ownership interest
in the real property for which an application is made; or
      2.   A person who is appealing a disciplinary action to the civil service
board; or
      3.   A person who is appealing a decision of the retirement system
manager to the retirement hearing commission; or
      4.   A person with a financial interest in the outcome of the decision of
the board which will exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). (Prior code §
53.03.024)
2.16.150   In addition to Political Reform Act of 1974.
   The provisions of this article are in addition to the conflict of interest
provisions in the Political Reform Act of 1974 (Government_Code Sections 87100,
et seq.) and the conflict of interest codes for the city boards and
commissions, and the city council. (Prior code § 53.03.025)
Article IV. City Employees
2.16.160   Applicability.
   The provisions of this article shall apply to each designated employee
required to file a statement disclosing financial interest pursuant to the
conflict of interest code adopted by the city council for his or her department
pursuant to the provisions of the Political Reform Act of 1974 (Government_Code
Sections 81000, et seq.). (Prior code § 53.04.030)
2.16.170   Disqualification.
   A.   Each city employee shall disqualify him or herself from making or
participating in the making of any decision when he or she knows or in the
exercise of reasonable diligence should know that:
      1.   Another person, with whom the city employee has an ownership
interest in real property or an investment in a business entity, is an
applicant or is principally involved in a matter before the department in which
the city employee is employed, or the city council or any board or commission
of the city; or
      2.   A family relative is an applicant or is principally involved in a
matter before the department in which the city employee is employed, or the
city council or any board or commission of the city.
   B.   No such city employee shall be prevented from making or participating
in the making of any decision to the extent his or her participation is legally
required for the decision to be made.
   C.   No such city employee shall make or participate in making a decision on
a matter for which disqualification is required under subsection A of this
section. (Prior code § 53.04.031)
2.16.180   Manner of disqualification.
   A city employee required to disqualify him or herself shall give written
notice of disqualification to the city clerk, to his or her immediate
supervisor and to his or her division head or department head if there is no
division head. The notice of disqualification shall include the name of the
applicant or person principally involved in the matter before the department,
and: (1) whether the city employee has an interest in real property or an
investment in a business entity with such person; or (2) who is a family
relative. Such notice shall be given as soon as is reasonably possible after
said employee learns, or, in the exercise of reasonable diligence should have
learned, of the facts requiring disqualification and shall be made part of the
official records of the city clerk. The city employee shall refrain from
participation and shall not attempt in any way to use his or her official
position to influence any other person with respect to the matter. (Prior code
§ 53.04.032)
2.16.190   Opinion of city attorney.
   Upon request, any city employee who is unsure of any right or obligation
arising under this code may request a formal opinion or letter of advice from
the city attorney. If an opinion is rendered by the city attorney stating in
full the facts and the law upon which the opinion is based, compliance by the
city employee may be evidence of good faith in any civil or criminal proceeding
brought pursuant to law. (Prior code § 53.04.033)
2.16.200   Definitions.
   For purposes of this article, the following terms have the meanings
specified:
   "Board" shall have the meaning specified in Section
2.16.140 of this chapter.
   "Business entity" shall have the meaning specified in Section
2.16.140 of this chapter.
   "City employee" means any employee identified in Section
2.16.160 of this chapter.
   "Family relative" shall have the meaning specified in Section
2.16.140 of this chapter.
   Investment in business entity:
      1.   Includes any financial interest in or security issued by a business
entity, including, but not limited to, common stock, preferred stock, rights,
warrants, options, deed instruments and any partnership or other ownership
interest; and
      2.   Applies to any investment, regardless of where such business entity
is located or does business; and
      3.   Applies to a city employee, if the employee and the person who is an
applicant or is principally involved in the matter before such city employee's
department, the city council or any board, each have a twenty-five thousand
dollar ($25,000.00) or greater, or ten (10) percent or greater, investment in
such business entity.
   "Ownership interest in real property" means and includes any leasehold
beneficial or ownership interest or option to acquire such an interest in real
property regardless of where such property is located, if the city employee and
the person who is an applicant or is principally involved in the matter before
such city employee's department, the city council or any board each have a
twenty-five thousand dollar ($25,000.00) or greater, or ten (10) percent or
greater, interest in such property.
   "Principally involved" means and includes:
      1.   A person who has a twenty-five (25) percent or greater investment in
the business entity, or a twenty-five (25) percent or greater ownership
interest in the real property for which an application is made; or
      2.   A person who is appealing a disciplinary action to the civil service
board; or
      3.   A person with a financial interest in the outcome of the decision of
the city employee's department, the city council or any board which will exceed
five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). (Prior code § 53.04.034)
2.16.210   In addition to Political Reform Act of 1974.
   The provisions of this article are in addition to the conflict of interest
provisions in the Political Reform Act of 1974 (Government_Code Sections 87100,
et seq.) and the conflict of interest codes for the various departments of the
city and any other city ordinance or other provision of law relating to
conflicts of interest. (Prior code § 53.04.035)
Chapter 2.18
OFFICE OF THE CITY AUDITOR
Sections:
2.18.010   Office of the city auditor.
2.18.020   City auditor qualifications.
2.18.030   Work plan and standards.
2.18.040   City auditor reports.
2.18.050   Duties of the city auditor.
2.18.060   Access to information.
2.18.070   Noninterference with city auditor.
2.18.010   Office of the city auditor.
   A.   The purposes of the city auditor's office are to independently assess
and report on city operations and services, assist the council in the conduct
of budgetary inquiries, assist the council in the making of budgetary
decisions, and to discharge other duties as prescribed by law or council
resolution.
   B.   The city auditor shall have such staff and budget as the city council
may prescribe.
   C.   The city auditor shall appoint all other members of the city auditor's
office. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-031 § 2)
2.18.020   City auditor qualifications.
   The city auditor shall be a certified public accountant, a certified
internal auditor, or have such other or additional qualifications as the city
council may establish by resolution. The city auditor shall set the
qualifications for subordinate staff. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-031 § 2)
2.18.030   Work plan and standards.
   A.   By April 15th each year, the city auditor shall submit an annual work
plan to the city council for approval. The annual work plan may be amended
during the year with the approval of the city council. The council may, by
resolution, authorize a committee, charter officer, or an individual
councilmember with respect to the councilmember's own office, to request
additional work.
   B.   Audits shall be conducted in accordance with Generally Accepted
Government Auditing Standards (GA-GAS) promulgated by the Comptroller General
of the United States of America or as otherwise prescribed by council
resolution.
   C.   The city auditor's office shall be subject to a peer review in
accordance with applicable government auditing standards at least once every
three years. A copy of the written report of this review shall be furnished to
the city council. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-031 § 2)
2.18.040   City auditor reports.
   A.   The city auditor shall prepare a written report of the results of each
audit conducted and will be responsible for retaining a copy as a permanent
record.
   B.   The city auditor shall periodically review audit recommendations and
investigations as practical to determine if responsive action has been taken.
The city auditor may request status reports from audit subjects regarding
actions taken to address audit findings and recommendations.
   C.   The council may prescribe by resolution the manner of report
preparation and presentation. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-031 § 2)
2.18.050   Duties of the city auditor.
   A.   The city auditor shall conduct audits of city departments, offices,
boards, commissions, and committees as directed by the council. Audits may be
conducted for the following purposes:
      1.   Determining if city activities and programs have been authorized by
applicable law or regulation, and are being conducted in compliance with
applicable laws and regulations;
      2.   Evaluating if a department, office, board, commission, or committee
is acquiring, managing, protecting, and using its resources economically,
efficiently, equitably, and effectively;
      3.   Determining whether city programs, activities, functions, or
policies are effective, including identification of any causes of
inefficiencies or uneconomical practices;
      4.   Evaluating whether financial and other reports fairly, accurately,
and fully disclose all information required by law, and determining whether
there are appropriate bases for evaluating programs and activities, including
the collection of, accounting for, and depositing of revenues and other
resources; and
      5.   Determining if city departments and offices have established
adequate operating and administrative procedures and practices, and internal
control systems.
   B.   The city auditor shall manage the city's whistleblower hotline and
determine if allegations of fraud, waste, abuse, or illegal acts need further
investigation.
   C.   As directed by the city council, the city auditor shall assist the
council's budgetary inquiries and budgetary decisions by:
      1.   Gathering, organizing, and analyzing data and information relative
to budgetary issues;
      2.   Providing comparative studies of other cities;
      3.   Analyzing the city's past, current, and proposed revenues and
expenditures;
      4.   Reviewing existing and potential tax revenues;
      5.   Analyzing federal, state, and local programs to determine sources of
funding and appropriate expenditure options;
      6.   Reviewing the economic and fiscal effects of proposed legislation;
      7.   Constructing economic models and indices;
      8.   Preparing fiscal and economic analysis of city projects;
      9.   Providing policy research and fiscal analysis on proposed
legislation; and
      10.   Preparing other reports relating to budgetary, economic, fiscal,
and legislative policy concerns.
   D.   The city auditor shall make recommendations to the city council in
connection with the city auditor's audits, investigations, analyses, studies,
and reports.
   E.   If an individual councilmember has requested an audit of that
councilmember's own office, the city auditor shall retain an independent
outside auditor to conduct the audit. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-031 § 2)
2.18.060   Access to information.
   A.   City departments, offices, and employees shall provide the city auditor
access to all sources of information, property, and personnel relevant to the
performance of an audit, unless restricted or prohibited by law. This section
shall not apply to the office of any elected official, unless that elected
official requested the audit of that official's own office.
   B.   If a city contract so provides, the city auditor shall have access to
the contracting party's employees, financial records, performance-related
records, property, and equipment related to the services or goods provided
under the contract. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-031 § 2)
2.18.070   Noninterference with city auditor.
   No person shall directly or indirectly coerce or attempt to coerce the city
auditor relative to the city auditor's examinations, audits, or the appointment
or removal of any employee by the city auditor. (Ord. 2019-0023 § 1; Ord. 2009-
031 § 2)
Chapter 2.20
POLICE DEPARTMENT
Sections:
2.20.010   Willful giving of false, misleading, etc., information.
2.20.020   Marksmanship badge-Established.
2.20.030   Marksmanship badge-Specifications.
2.20.040   Marksmanship badge-Presentation.
2.20.060   Blowing or imitating police officer's whistle.
2.20.070   Reserve police officer-Designated and non-designated.
2.20.010   Willful giving of false, misleading, etc., information.
   It is unlawful for any person to knowingly and willfully furnish, give or
make a false, misleading or unfounded report to the police department for the
purpose of interfering with proper operation of the police department or any of
its officers or both. (Prior code § 30.01.001)
2.20.020   Marksmanship badge-Established.
   A system of official badges for marksmanship to be worn by the members of
the police department who have earned them is established. The medal shall
consist of a medallion and bar pin which shall indicate the rank attained in
the practice test. This bar shall be changed from year to year to indicate such
rank. (Prior code § 30.01.004)
2.20.030   Marksmanship badge-Specifications.
   The specifications for the medallion and bars of the marksmanship medals
shall be as follows:
   A.   A medallion of sterling silver, one and one-eighth inches in diameter
and three thirty-seconds inch thick with two substantial closed links attached
to upper edge as shown in cut. The front and reverse sides shall be stamped
with design and lettering as shown in cut.
   B.   A gold bar pin, ten (10) carat, one and three-sixteenths inches long by
five-sixteenths inch wide by three sixty-fourths inch thick with two closed
links attached to lower edge. The front side of the bar shall be stamped with
design as shown in cut and the word "EXPERT" and the year of issue to be in
raised letters and numerals as shown in cut. The back side of the bar shall
have soldered on it a substantial pin with safety catch.
   C.   A sterling silver bar pin, same dimensions and construction as the gold
bar pin; except, the front side will contain the word "SHARPSHOOTER" and the
year of issue in raised letters together with the design as shown in the cut.
   D.   A bronze bar pin, same dimensions and construction as the gold and
silver bar pins; except, that the front side will contain the word "MARKSMAN"
and the year of issue in raised letters together with the design as shown in
the cut. (Prior code § 30.01.005)
   Editor's note: The "cuts" for designs of marksmanship medals referred to in
the above section will be found on file in the office of the chief of police.
2.20.040   Marksmanship badge-Presentation.
   Such marksmanship medals shall be purchased by the city and shall be
presented to such members of the police department as may from year to year
qualify in the respective ratings according to the rules adopted therefor by
the chief of police and approved by the city manager. (Prior code § 30.01.006)
2.20.060   Blowing or imitating police officer's whistle.
   It is unlawful for any person not a peace officer to blow any police
officer's whistle or to make anywhere within the city limits any noise
imitating a police officer's whistle or to do any act or thing to lead any
person to believe he or she is a police officer or other peace officer. (Prior
code § 30.01.008)
2.20.070   Reserve police officer-Designated and non-designated.
   A.   The chief of police, or authorized designee, has the authority to
select and appoint any reserve police officer within the "Reserve Police
Officer I" job classification as a "designated" reserve police officer as
provided by California Penal_Code Section 830.6(a)(2). The authority of the
reserve police officer so designated includes the full powers and duties of a
peace officer as provided by California Penal_Code Section 830.1.
   B.   Any reserve police officer within the "Reserve Police Officer I" job
classification not appointed as a "designated" reserve police officer as
provided in subsection A of this section is a "non-designated" reserve police
officer as provided by California Penal_Code Section 830.6(a)(1). The authority
of a non-designated reserve police officer shall extend only for the duration
of the reserve officer's specific assignment. (Ord. 2012-006 § 2)
Chapter 2.22
OFFICE OF PUBLIC SAFETY ACCOUNTABILITY
Sections:
2.22.010   Office of public safety accountability created.
2.22.020   Office of public safety accountability director qualifications.
2.22.030   Duties and functions of office.
2.22.040   Office of public safety accountability reports.
2.22.050   Access to information.
2.22.010   Office of public safety accountability created.
   There is created an office of public safety accountability, to be headed by
a director appointed by the city council. The director shall be a city officer
under Section
70, subdivision (d), of the charter. The office shall have such staff and
budget as the city council may prescribe. The director shall appoint all other
members of the office. (Ord. 2016-0054 § 2)
2.22.020   Office of public safety accountability director qualifications.
   The city council may establish the director's qualifications by resolution.
The director shall set the qualifications for subordinate staff. (Ord. 2016-
0054 § 2)
2.22.030   Duties and functions of office.
   The office shall:
   A.   Audit all complaint investigations of the police department and fire
department, as the director deems necessary.
   B.   Monitor all complaint investigations conducted by the police department
and fire department.
   C.   Request the police department and fire department perform further
investigation in those complaint cases that require additional investigation as
determined by the director.
   D.   Receive all documents, reports, or any other item necessary to monitor
or audit a complaint investigation.
   E.   Assist the city council, or any duly appointed committee of the
council, in performing its investigative functions under section
34 of the charter.
   F.   As needed, request the city council, or any duly appointed committee of
the council, to issue subpoenas as provided in section
34 of the charter. The city council may, by resolution, establish the
procedures for the request, issuance, and service of those subpoenas.
   G.   Perform such other inquiries and investigations as prescribed by
council resolution.
   H.   Accept and document complaints directly from citizens as an alternative
procedure for citizen complaints concerning public safety personnel, using a
complaint form distinct from that used by the police department or fire
department. All such complaints shall be promptly forwarded to the respective
public safety department for investigation.
   I.   Provide complainants with timely updates on the status of
investigations, excluding disclosure of any information that is confidential or
legally protected.
   J.   Explain how the complaint process works to all complainants.
   K.   Monitor or independently investigate any other matter as directed by
the city council pursuant to section
34 of the charter.
   L.   Serve in a public information capacity, including providing public
information, excluding disclosure of any information that is confidential or
legally protected, on pending investigations as directed by the city council;
and making presentations in community forums.
   M.   Respond to critical incidents involving police or fire personnel and
provide a report to city council regarding the details and concerns of those
incidents. (Ord. 2016-0054 § 2)
2.22.040   Office of public safety accountability reports.
   The director shall prepare written reports as directed by council or a duly
appointed committee of the council. The council may prescribe by resolution the
manner of report preparation and presentation. At a minimum, the director shall
prepare quarterly reports consistent with California Penal_Code section 832.7
(c), relating to the number, kind, and status of all citizen complaints filed
against police department personnel for review by the Sacramento community
police review commission and the city council. (Ord. 2016-0054 § 2)
2.22.050   Access to information.
   City departments, offices, and employees shall provide the office of public
safety accountability access to all sources of information, property, and
personnel relevant to the performance of the office's duties under this
chapter, unless restricted or prohibited by law. (Ord. 2016-0054 § 2)
Chapter 2.24
FIRE DEPARTMENT
Sections:
2.24.010   Powers and duties of the fire chief.
2.24.020   Organization generally.
2.24.030   Tampering with fire alarm system.
2.24.040   False alarms-Reward for arrest of violators.
2.24.050   Obstructing fire alarm boxes.
2.24.060   Interference with wire of the fire alarm system resulting from the
moving of buildings.
2.24.070   Interference with lines of the telegraph system.
2.24.080   Emergency repairs by licensed contractors.
2.24.090   Application fees for permits and clearances issued by the fire
department.
2.24.100   Establishment of rates, fees or charges for emergency ambulance
services.
2.24.010   Powers and duties of the fire chief.
   The chief of the fire department shall exercise all the powers and perform
all the duties that are now or may hereafter be conferred upon him or her by
the provisions of the Charter, by ordinance or by the directions of the city
manager. He or she shall be appointed by, responsible to, and removable at the
pleasure of the city manager. He or she shall be responsible for the government
and discipline of the fire department and the members thereof and shall be
charged with the care and custody of all property and equipment belonging to
the department. He or she shall make a special study of the fire preventive
measures and shall from time to time make a report of his or her findings and
recommendations in order that proper legislation might be enacted in the
premises and the people educated to assist in the prevention of fires. (Prior
code § 15.01.101)
2.24.020   Organization generally.
   In addition to the chief of the fire department and the two assistant chiefs
of the fire department, there shall be captains, inspectors of the bureau of
fire prevention, engineers and firefighters, as may be necessary to carry out
the provisions of the two-platoon system; providing, however, that for each
platoon of the fire department, there shall be for each engine company, one
captain, one engineer and not less than five firefighters; for each truck
company, one captain and not less than seven firefighters; for each chemical
company, one captain and not less than two firefighters; and, there may also be
two relief engineers of the fire department.
   Inspectors of the bureau of fire prevention shall have civil service
classification within the fire department, and shall receive the same salary as
firefighters. (Prior code § 15.01.102)
2.24.030   Tampering with fire alarm system.
   No person shall break, remove or injure any of the parts or appurtenances of
the fire alarm system without authority or permission of the chief of the fire
department. No person shall make or fit any key to the lock of any signal box
of the fire alarm system without authority of the chief of the fire department.
No person shall have or retain in his or her possession or under his or her
control a key belonging to or fitted to open the lock of any such signal box
without lawful authority of the fire chief. No person shall force or pick the
lock of any such signal box without the authority of the fire chief. (Prior
code § 15.01.104)
2.24.040   False alarms-Reward for arrest of violators.
   No person shall willfully make or cause to be made any false alarm of fire
by means of the fire alarm system, or otherwise. A reward of twenty-five
dollars ($25.00) will be paid by the city council for the arrest and conviction
of any person for giving, by means of the fire alarm system, a false alarm of
fire. (Prior code § 15.01.105)
2.24.050   Obstructing fire alarm boxes.
   No person shall put or place, maintain or suffer to be or remain any
article, thing or matter on or upon the sidewalk so as to obstruct or interfere
with the free access or approach to any signal box of the fire alarm system.
(Prior code § 15.01.106)
2.24.060   Interference with wire of the fire alarm system resulting from the
moving of buildings.
   Any person moving, or intending to move, any house, structure or building
likely to interfere with the fire alarm system shall at once give notice to the
chief of the fire department, and shall at once make provision for the
immediate repair of any injury or of any disturbance of such fire alarm system;
provided, that no interference for such cause shall take place between the
hours of five
p.m. in the evening and eight a.m. in the morning. (Prior code § 15.01.107)
2.24.070   Interference with lines of the telegraph system.
   No person shall run any wire on any of the telegraph poles or fixtures of
the fire alarm system of this city, or run, erect or maintain any wire crossing
or running parallel to any wire of the fire alarm system within a distance of
six feet. No person shall, with intent to deceive, falsely represent himself or
herself to be an employee of the fire alarm system of the city. No person
owning or controlling property along the lines of the fire alarm system shall
allow any branch or limb of any tree, shrub or vine to be within six feet of
the fire alarm system. (Prior code § 15.01.108)
2.24.080   Emergency repairs by licensed contractors.
   The chief of the fire department is authorized to allow qualified licensed
contractors to enter upon any property within the city in order to make
emergency repairs and furnish materials to protect buildings, structures,
dwellings, and their contents and surrounding premises that have been damaged
or placed at risk by fire, explosion, flood or other casualty from further loss
or damage, or to eliminate any hazard to the public health or safety that
exists by reason of such damage or risk to such property; provided, however,
that the foregoing shall not authorize the payment of any public monies by or
on behalf of the city for the performance by any contractor or person of the
services hereinabove described.
   The chief of the fire department shall promulgate standards for selecting
qualified contractors and rules under which said contractors shall perform the
services hereinabove described. Said standards and rules shall be adopted by
and may be amended by resolution of the city council. (Prior code § 15.01.110)
2.24.090   Application fees for permits and clearances issued by the fire
department.
   The fire department shall charge fees to defray its administrative costs,
including, but not limited to, inspections by fire department personnel, in
connection with all applications for a permit or clearance, or annual renewal
thereof, required under the Uniform Fire Code, the California Health_and_Safety
Code, Title 19 of the California_Administrative_Code, or the Sacramento City
Code. The fees shall be set by resolution of the city council and shall be
charged and collected at the time an application for a permit or clearance is
made. The application fee shall not be refunded upon failure of an applicant to
receive a permit or clearance or upon any revocation or suspension of a permit
or clearance. No permit or clearance shall be valid until the required fee has
been paid to the city revenue officer. (Prior code § 15.01.111)
2.24.100   Establishment of rates, fees or charges for emergency ambulance
services.
   A.   The city council shall set rates, fees and charges for emergency
ambulance services by resolution.
   B.   Every person receiving emergency ambulance services from the city shall
be liable for the rates, fees and charges for that service, as established by
resolution of the city council.
   C.   Bills for emergency ambulance services shall be due upon presentation
of the bill for services. Charges unpaid ninety (90) days after presentation
become past due. Charges that remain unpaid thirty (30) days following the past
due date shall be assessed a five percent penalty. Interest shall accrue on any
charges unpaid from the past due date until paid at the rate of one percent per
month.
   D.   The rates, fees and charges imposed for ambulance service shall not
exceed city's estimated actual cost to provide emergency ambulance service.
(Prior code § 15.01.112)
Chapter 2.28
DEPARTMENT OF COMMUNITY SERVICES
Sections:
2.28.010   Department of community services.

shall continue to be the director of community services who shall serve at the

The director of community services shall exercise supervision and control over
the work, operating services and activities of the department of community

Sections:

Chapter 2.40
BOARDS AND COMMISSION GENERALLY*
Sections:
Article I. General
2.40.010   Definitions.
2.40.020   Intent.
Article II. Appointment Procedures

2.40.050   Procedures for concurrence in appointments to boards and
commissions.

Article III. Members of Boards and Commissions
2.40.070   Applicability.
2.40.080   Failure to attend meetings.
2.40.090   Terms.

2.40.110   Eligibility.
2.40.120   Removal of members for failure to comply with the law.
Article IV. Meetings of Boards and Commissions
2.40.130   Applicability.
2.40.140   Meetings generally.
2.40.150   Voting.
2.40.155   Quorum.
2.40.160   Ad hoc committees and subcommittees.
2.40.170   Chairperson and vice-chairperson.
2.40.180   City clerk is secretary.
2.40.190   City attorney is legal counsel.
2.40.200   Review of boards and commissions.
*   Prior history: prior code §§ 60.01.001-60.01.008, 60.02.010, 60.02.011,
60.03.015, 60.04.017, 60.04.018 and Ords. 2019-011, 2017-0026, 2016-0055, 2016-
0036, 2015-0026, 2012-0048, 2012-004, 2009-045, 2008-001, 2006-065 and 2006-
041.
Article I. General
2.40.010   Definitions.
   The following definitions apply in this chapter:
   "Boards and commissions" means all boards, commissions, and committees with
members who are appointed by the mayor or the city council. "Boards and
commissions" includes city boards and commissions. "Boards and commissions"
does not include committees that are composed solely of members of the city
council.
   "City boards and commissions" means boards, commissions, and committees
established by the charter, ordinance, or resolution. "City boards and
commissions" does not include committees that are composed solely of members of
city council. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.020   Intent.
   It is the intent of the city council, in enacting this chapter, to assure
that appointees for seats on boards and commissions possess those high ethical
standards required of them to properly fulfill their functions; to disclose any
conflicts of interest that would render applicants and appointees ineffective
in the performance of their duties, or which would jeopardize the interests of
the city; to protect applicants and appointees against untrue allegations with
respect to their background and integrity; and to establish a uniform
administrative framework for all city boards and commissions. (Ord. 2022-0024 §
2)
Article II. Appointment Procedures
2.40.040   Applications.
   Except for members of the city council and city employees appointed in the
capacity of their employment, each person seeking appointment to a seat on any
board or commission shall submit an application on a form supplied by the city
clerk. The application shall be submitted in a manner prescribed by the city
clerk. The application must require information or documentation to effectuate
the intent of this chapter, consistent with requirements of the law, including
this code, ordinances, and resolutions. The application shall be signed by the
applicant under penalty of perjury. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.050   Procedures for concurrence in appointments to boards and
commissions.
   A.   The mayor, individual councilmembers, or the Personnel and Public
Employees Committee shall recommend persons for board and commission
appointments as specified elsewhere by ordinance, resolution, or this code.
   B.   Concurrence in an appointment for a seat on a city board or commission
shall be by vote of the city council.
   C.   A concurrence vote on an appointee for a seat on a city board or
commission shall not be taken unless the appointee has filed with the city
clerk the application required by section
2.40.040. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 2; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.060   Vacancies.
   A.   If a seat on a board or commission becomes vacant during a member's
term, the vacancy shall be filled in the same manner that a member is required
to be initially appointed to that seat, pursuant to this code, ordinance, or
resolution.
   B.   If, at the end of a member's term, the member is not reappointed and a
successor is not appointed, the member may continue to serve until they are
reappointed or a successor is appointed, if it is determined by the
recommending authority that an extended term would be advantageous to continue
ongoing work or because the commission is experiencing challenges establishing
a quorum. As used in this subsection, "recommending authority" means, as
applicable, the mayor, councilmember, or for a member recommended for
appointment by the Personnel and Public Employees Committee, the chair of that
committee. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 3; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
Article III. Members of Boards and Commissions
2.40.070   Applicability.
   Despite any other contrary provision of this code, an ordinance, or a
resolution, this article applies to members of any board or commission who are
appointed by the mayor or the city council. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.080   Failure to attend meetings.
   A.   Three absences from regular meetings in a calendar year is deemed good
cause for removal of a board or commission member from office under the
provisions of section
232 of the Sacramento City Charter.
   B.   The city clerk shall send a written communication to a board or
commission member after their third absence in a calendar year. The city clerk
shall thereafter consult with that board or commission member's recommending
authority before commencing the removal process under section
232 of the Sacramento City Charter. As used in this subsection, "recommending
authority" means, as applicable, the mayor, councilmember, or for a member
recommended for appointment by the Personnel and Public Employees Committee,
the chair of that committee.
   C.   For purposes of counting absences under this section:
      1.   The failure to attend a meeting by any board or commission member on
account of the performance of their official city duties does not count as an
absence.
      2.   A board or commission member will be counted as absent if they fail
to attend a meeting for a majority of the duration of the meeting. (Ord. 2024-
0042 § 4; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.090   Terms.
   A.   Terms generally.
      1.   Except as otherwise provided in this section, the term of each seat
on a city board or commission is four years.
      2.   The term of each designated youth seat on a city board or commission
is two years.
   B.   The term for a member recommended for appointment by the mayor or a
councilmember expires on the same date as the term of office of the
recommending mayor or councilmember. Terms are not automatically extended due
to the re-election of the recommending mayor or councilmember.
   C.   This section does not apply to the following:
      1.   City board and commission seats to which members were appointed
before July 1, 2022;
      2.   Seats on city boards and commissions for which terms are otherwise
provided in the charter; and
      3.   The Sacramento Youth Commission.
(Ord. 2024-0042 § 5; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.100   Limitation on number of consecutive terms served.
   A.   No person appointed to any board or commission may be appointed to
serve more than two consecutive terms on that same board or commission.
   B.   Subsection A of this section shall not apply:
      1.   If the appointee is the mayor or a member of the city council;
      2.   If the appointee is appointed jointly by the mayor or city council
and any other appointing authority;
      3.   If the board or commission is established by the charter; or
      4.   If the appointee is a city employee who is appointed in the capacity
of their employment.
   C.   A member appointed to complete 75% or more of an unexpired term shall
be eligible to serve up to two consecutive terms; the unexpired term will be
considered as the first full term of the two consecutive full terms. A member
appointed to complete less than 75% of an unexpired term shall be eligible to
serve up to two full consecutive terms in addition to the partial unexpired
term.
   D.   A person who is prohibited from being appointed to a consecutive term
pursuant to subsection A above is eligible for reappointment to that same board
or commission two years after the last date the member served on that same
board or commission. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 6; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.110   Eligibility.
   A.   City employees are ineligible to be members of boards or commissions,
unless they are appointed in the capacity of their employment.
   B.   All members appointed to the City's boards and commissions must be
residents of the City of Sacramento and remain residents for the entirety of
their term. This subsection B does not apply to members of the Sacramento Youth
Commission or the Preservation Commission.
   C.   A member removed from a board or commission for violation of sections
2.40.080 or
2.40.120 may not be appointed to any city board or commission for one year from
the date of their removal.
   D.   No person may be appointed to serve on more than one board or
commission concurrently. This subsection D does not apply to members of the
Sacramento Relocation Appeals Board. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 7; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.120   Removal of members for failure to comply with the law.
   A.   Each member of a board or commission shall comply with all laws or
requirements relating to the member's office (including provisions of any
resolution, ordinance, or local, state or federal law).This includes, but is
not limited to the following:
      1.   Taking and subscribing the oath or affirmation for public officers
(Cal. Const., art. XX, § 3);
      2.   Filing a statement of economic interests, if required by the city's
conflict of interest code adopted pursuant to the Political Reform Act (Cal.
Gov. Code, § 81000 et seq.); and
      3.   Completing training in general ethics principles and ethics laws
(Cal. Gov. Code, § 53235).
   B.   For purposes of charter section
232, a failure of any member of a board or commission to comply with subsection
A is deemed good cause for removal from office. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
Article IV. Meetings of Boards and Commissions
2.40.130   Applicability.
   This article applies to all city boards and commissions, despite any other
contrary provision of this code, ordinance, or resolution. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.140   Meetings generally.
   A.   Each regular meeting of a city board or commission shall be noticed and
held in accordance with the provisions of sections 4.04.020.A and
4.04.030.
   B.   Each meeting shall be conducted in accordance with the Council Rules of
Procedure.
   C.   If a quorum is not established within 15 minutes after the meeting's
noticed start time, the meeting shall be cancelled.
   D.   With the approval by the city clerk, city boards and commissions may
notice and hold special meetings in accordance with the Ralph M. Brown Act
(Cal. Gov. Code, § 54950 et seq.). (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.150   Voting.
   A.   On all matters voted upon by each city board or commission, the ayes,
nays, and members present and not voting shall be entered upon the minutes or
other record of the meeting by the city clerk or secretary.
   B.   To vote, a member must be physically present at the dais at the
designated meeting location or at a properly noticed teleconference location.
Proxy or absentee voting is not permitted. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 8; Ord. 2022-0024
§ 2)
2.40.155   Quorum.
   A majority of the number of seats established for a board or commission
constitutes a quorum. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 9)
2.40.160   Ad hoc committees and subcommittees.
   A.   City boards and commissions may have ad hoc committees, subject to the
restrictions of the Ralph M. Brown Act (Cal. Gov. Code, § 54950 et seq.) and
city administrative policy for those ad hoc committees.
   B.   A city board or commission may establish a subcommittee upon approval
by the city council. Before consideration by the city council, the city board
or commission must make its request to establish a subcommittee to the
Personnel and Public Employees Committee.
   C.   A subcommittee of a city board or commission shall comply with the
following:
      1.   Subcommittee appointments shall be made by the chairperson of the
city board or commission.
      2.   A subcommittee is a city legislative body subject to the Ralph M.
Brown Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 54950 et seq.) and the Sacramento Sunshine
Ordinance (Sacramento City Code
chapter 4.04).
      3.   A city board or commission member who is not a member of the
subcommittee may attend a subcommittee meeting, provided the member attends
only as an observer, does not testify or otherwise participate in any
discussion, and sits amongst the public.
   D.   The city clerk shall assign staff to assist subcommittees with their
operations. (Ord. 2024-0042 § 10; Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.170   Chairperson and vicechairperson.
   A.   Each city board and commission shall elect one of its members to serve
as chairperson and another to serve as vicechairperson for each calendar year.
A member may serve as the chairperson or vicechairperson for no more than two
calendar years.
   B.   The chairperson shall be the presiding officer and shall ensure the
orderly conduct of the meeting.
   C.   If the chairperson is absent, the vicechairperson shall act in the
capacity of the chairperson. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.180   City clerk is secretary.
   Pursuant to charter section
71, the city clerk shall act as secretary of city boards and commissions. (Ord.
2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.190   City attorney is legal counsel.
   Pursuant to charter section
72, the city attorney shall serve as legal counsel to city boards and
commissions. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
2.40.200   Review of boards and commissions.
   At least every five years, the city clerk shall report on the status of
boards and commissions to the Personnel and Public Employees Committee. This
report may include, but is not limited to, recommendations to amend the
membership requirements, to amend the scope of the body's authority, or to
dissolve the body. (Ord. 2022-0024 § 2)
Chapter 2.48
CITY OF SACRAMENTO CONSTRUCTION CODE ADVISORY AND APPEALS BOARD
Sections:
2.48.010   Board established.
2.48.020   Purpose of board.
2.48.030   Powers and duties of board.
2.48.040   Appointment of members and qualifications.
2.48.050   General provisions.
2.48.010   Board established.
   The City of Sacramento Construction Code Advisory and Appeals Board is
hereby established. (Ord. 2024-0028 § 1)
2.48.020   Purpose of board.
   The board is established for the purpose of hearing appeals of decisions,
orders, and determinations of the chief building official, and granting
variances as provided elsewhere in this code. (Ord. 2024-0028 § 1)
2.48.030   Powers and duties of board.
   The powers and duties of the board are as follows:
   A.   The board shall hear appeals of decisions, orders, or determinations of
the chief building official relating to application and interpretation of the
Sacramento City Building Code, any building standards published in the
California Building Standards Code, or any other applicable rule or regulation
adopted by the California Department of Housing and Community Development,
including decisions, orders, or determinations that concern the use of any
material, alternate design, or method of construction not specifically
prescribed by the California Building Standards Code.
   B.   The board may grant variances as provided elsewhere in this code. (Ord.
2024-0028 § 1)
2.48.040   Appointment of members and qualifications.
   A.   Number of members. The board has five members.
      1.   The Personnel and Public Employees Committee shall recommend five
members for appointment:
         a.   At least one member must be a California licensed general
building contractor who was a general contractor on more than one construction
project in the city during the two years immediately preceding appointment;
         b.   At least one member must be a California licensed architect who
has practiced in California for at least three years immediately preceding
appointment;
         c.   The remaining three members of the board may consist of any
combination of the following: California licensed general building contractors
as specified in subsection A.1.a above; California licensed architects as
specified in subsection A.1.b above; or any of the following:
            i.   A California registered structural engineer who has practiced
in California for at least three years immediately preceding appointment;
            ii.   A California registered fire protection engineer who has
practiced in California for at least three years immediately preceding
appointment;
            iii.   A California registered mechanical engineer who has
practiced in California for at least three years immediately preceding
appointment;
            iv.   A California licensed plumbing contractor who has practiced
in California for at least three years immediately preceding appointment;
            v.   A California licensed mechanical contractor who has practiced
in California for at least three years immediately preceding appointment;
            vi.   A California registered electrical engineer who has practiced
in California for at least three years immediately preceding appointment; or
            vii.   A California licensed electrical contractor who has
practiced in California for at least three years immediately preceding
appointment.
   B.   Qualifications. In addition to any requirements or restrictions in
chapter 2.40:
      1.   Members must have an expressed interest or demonstrated history of
involvement in the California Building Standards Code and the city building
code. (Ord. 2024-0028 § 1)
2.48.050   General provisions.
   Unless specifically provided otherwise in this chapter, the provisions of
chapter 2.40 apply to the board and its members. (Ord. 2024-0028 § 1)

Chapter 2.53
CITY OF SACRAMENTO DISABILITIES ADVISORY COMMISSION
Sections:
2.53.010   Commission established.
2.53.020   Purposes of commission.
2.53.030   Powers and duties of commission.
2.53.040   Appointment of members and qualifications.
2.53.050   General provisions.
2.53.010   Commission established.
   The City of Sacramento Disabilities Advisory Commission is hereby
established. (Ord. 2024-0030 § 1)
2.53.020   Purposes of commission.
   The commission is established for the purpose of providing advice and
recommendations to the city council on strategies and policies designed to
ensure and enhance the city's compliance with the Americans with Disabilities
Act, the California Fair Employment and Housing Act, and Title 24 of the
California_Code_of_Regulations. (Ord. 2024-0030 § 1)
2.53.030   Powers and duties of commission.
   The powers and duties of the commission are as follows:
   A.   To advise the city council regarding compliance with federal and state
disability laws. The commission shall not advise the city concerning litigation
or administrative proceedings to which the city is a party;
   B.   To review policies, programs and activities within the city as they
affect persons with disabilities;
   C.   To recommend procedures for city employees with disabilities to request
and receive reasonable accommodations;
   D.   To provide information, referral and technical assistance to the city
in matters pertaining to disability issues;
   E.   To establish a liaison with the city's ADA coordinators to assist with
policies, procedures and programs as they relate to federal and state
disability laws.
   F.   Annually, report to and make recommendations to the city council
regarding the city's compliance with state and federal disability laws and
activities of the commission. (Ord. 2024-0030 § 1)
2.53.040   Appointment of members and qualifications.
   A.   Number of members. The commission shall consist of 11 members:
      1.   Each councilmember shall recommend one member for appointment (eight
members total);
      2.   The mayor shall recommend two members for appointment; and
      3.   The Personnel and Public Employees Committee shall recommend for
appointment one member, who must be at least 16 years old and not older than 22
years old at the time of appointment.
   B.   Qualifications. In addition to any requirements or restrictions in
chapter 2.40:
      1.   Members must have an expressed interest or demonstrated history in
disability issues, or knowledge or experience with disability law, such as the
Americans with Disabilities Act, the California Fair Employment and Housing
Act, and Title 24 of the California_Code_of_Regulations. (Ord. 2024-0030 § 1)
2.53.050   General provisions.
   Unless specifically provided otherwise in this chapter, the provisions of
chapter 2.40 apply to the commission and its members. (Ord. 2024-0030 § 1)
Chapter 2.56
SACRAMENTO RELOCATION APPEALS BOARD
Sections:
2.56.010   Creation of board.
2.56.020   Function of the board.
2.56.030   Members of the board.
2.56.040   Chairperson and organization of the board.
2.56.010   Creation of board.
   The Sacramento relocation appeals board is established. (Prior code §
60.13.110)
2.56.020   Function of the board.
   The function of the Sacramento relocation appeals board shall be:
   A.   To act as the relocation appeals board created in the city under the
provisions of the Community Redevelopment Law of the state of California as set
forth in Article XI, Chapter 4, Part I, Division 24 (Section 33417.5) of the
Health_and_Safety_Code.
   B.   To act as the relocation appeals board pursuant to the "regulations of
the city of Sacramento for relocation assistance to displaced persons,
families, business and farm operations," effective January 1, 1974, adopted by
the city council in compliance with statutes of 1972, Chapter 1307. (Prior code
§ 60.13.111)
2.56.030   Members of the board.
   The board shall consist of five members of the Sacramento housing and
redevelopment commission to be appointed by the mayor with the approval of the
city council. The term of office for each such member of the board shall
coincide with that member's term of office as a member of the Sacramento
housing and redevelopment commission. Members shall receive all actual and
necessary expenses, including travel expenses, incurred in the discharge of
their duties. (Prior code § 60.13.112)
2.56.040   Chairperson and organization of the board.
   The mayor with the approval of the city council shall appoint the first
chairperson of the board from among its members. When there is a vacancy in the
office of chairperson, the commission shall elect a chairperson from among its
members. A majority of the members of the board shall determine the time, place
and frequency of its meetings, and adopt rules of procedure for the conduct of
board hearings and business. The board shall act only by a majority vote of all
members. The board may do any other things necessary or proper to carry out its
functions. (Prior code § 60.13.113)
Chapter 2.58
CITY OF SACRAMENTO PRESERVATION COMMISSION
Sections:
2.58.010   Commission established.
2.58.020   Purpose of commission.
2.58.030   Powers and duties.
2.58.040   Appointment of members and qualifications.
2.58.050   General provisions.
2.58.010   Commission established.
   The City of Sacramento Preservation Commission is hereby established. (Ord.
2024-0031 § 1)
2.58.020   Purpose of commission.
   The commission is established for the purpose of providing advice and
recommendations to the city council on policies and programs in support of
historic preservation, including the goals and policies for the general plan
and updates of the preservation program, and to exercise the authority set
forth in this chapter and as otherwise provided in this code. (Ord. 2024-0031 §
1)
2.58.030   Powers and duties.
   The powers and duties of the commission are as follows:
   A.   Recommend to the city council policies and programs in support of
historic preservation, including goals and policies for the general plan
preservation element and other regulatory plans; periodic updates of the
preservation program, including the standards, criteria, and procedures set
forth in
chapter 17.604; and programs for historic preservation incentives.
   B.   Evaluate and submit comments and recommendations on proposed plans,
public and private development projects, and environmental reviews that are not
subject to review under
chapter 17.604 but that may potentially affect the physical development and
historic preservation of the city involving landmarks, contributing resources,
historic districts, nominated resources, or the historical value of any other
building, structure, or neighborhood, in coordination with review and action by
the city council, planning and design commission, or other public agencies on
the plan, project, or environmental review.
   C.   Review and make recommendation to the State Office of Historic
Preservation regarding nominations of property located within the city to the
National Register of Historic Places.
   D.   Assume duties assigned to the preservation commission by the city
council pursuant to the certified local government provisions of the National
Historic Preservation Act of 1966, or duties that may be assigned to the
preservation commission through any agreement(s) approved by the city council.
This shall include undertaking review and comment upon those projects on which
the city, as a certified local government, has an obligation or opportunity to
provide review and comment under the National Historic Preservation Act,
including private and public projects undertaken within the Old Sacramento
national historic landmark district.
   E.   Annually, report to and make recommendations to the city council
regarding the activities of the commission and the status of policies and
programs in support of historic preservation, including the goals and policies
for the general plan and updates of the preservation program in the city. (Ord.
2024-0031 § 1)
2.58.040   Appointment of members and qualifications.
   A.   The commission has seven members. The Personnel and Public Employees
Committee shall recommend all seven members for appointment.
   B.   Qualifications. In addition to any requirements or restrictions in
chapter 2.40:
      1.   Each member must have demonstrated knowledge of the Secretary of the
Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties and the
California Historical Building Code.
      2.   In addition, the seven members of the commission must be qualified
as follows:
         a.   One must be a licensed historical architect who meets the
Secretary of the Interior's qualifications for historical architects.
         b.   One must be an architectural historian with training or
experience in the architectural history of Sacramento, the Sacramento region,
Northern California, or the West and who meets the Secretary of the Interior's
qualifications for architectural historians.
         c.   One must be a registered structural engineer.
         d.   One must be a licensed contractor and who has training or
experience in restoration of historic properties.
         e.   One must be a landscape architect, designer, or historian with
training or experience in historical landscapes.
         f.   One is an at-large member, with a preference for an individual
with training or experience in historic preservation or urban planning.
         g.   One is an at-large member, with a preference for an individual
with training or experience in the history of Sacramento, the Sacramento
region, Northern California, or the West and who meets the Secretary of the
Interior's qualifications for historians.
      3.   Notwithstanding section
2.40.110.B, members of the commission need not be residents of the city;
however, there is a preference for persons who are city residents or who own a
business located in the city. (Ord. 2024-0031 § 1)
2.58.050   General provisions.
   Unless specifically provided otherwise in this chapter, the provisions of
chapter 2.40 apply to the commission and its members. (Ord. 2024-0031 § 1)

construction; urban planning; urban design; or mid- and high- rise urban,
commercial, institutional, and mixed-use projects.
         b.   Three must: (i) have demonstrated interest in urban design,

(ii) be qualified by training or professional experience and demonstrated
leadership in any of the following categories: a licensed architect; a licensed
LEED (or equivalent) architect; a licensed landscape architect; a licensed
contractor; or a licensed engineer.
   B.   Qualifications. In addition to any requirements or restrictions in
chapter 2.40:
      1.   Members must have an expressed interest, training, or experience in
master planning; land use or land use policy; housing policy; large scale
construction; urban planning; urban design; or mid- and high-rise urban,
commercial, institutional, and mixed-use projects. (Ord. 2024-0032 § 1)
2.60.045   Voting.
   The commission shall act only by motion. An affirmative vote of seven
members present and qualified to vote is necessary to pass any motion. (Ord.
2024-0032 § 1)
2.60.050   General provisions.
   Unless specifically provided otherwise in this chapter, the provisions of
chapter 2.40 apply to the commission and its members. (Ord. 2024-0032 § 1)
